Subject: Multiparametric MRI Prostate | Antoni van Leeuwenhoek | 10 Jan 2025
Clinical indication: Specialist review for PSA escalation to 17.0 ng/mL after an earlier negative biopsy.

Volume measures 48.89 mL. A right mid-gland peripheral zone focus spans 12 x 8 x 10 mm. T2-weighted sequences highlight pronounced hypointensity. Diffusion imaging exhibits high signal intensity alongside correspondingly depressed ADC values. Dynamic contrast enhancement shows early focal uptake. There is no evidence of extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, suspicious lymphadenopathy, or osseous lesions.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right mid-gland peripheral zone.
PSAD 0.35 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.86317605

previous_notes.author: Dr. M. Jansen (GP)
previous_notes.text: 18 May 2024 - Dr. M. Jansen (GP): Laboratory results indicate the patient’s PSA climbed to 14.5 ng/mL subsequent to his initial negative biopsy earlier this year. Due to this upward trajectory and his age, a referral to urology was processed for specialist re-evaluation and additional imaging. He notes persistent mild lower urinary tract symptoms but explicitly denies haematuria or pelvic discomfort.
